title: Deception entitlement: the Client Connector integration, the enabled-by-default switch, user and device groups, the logout option and update timing
aliases: enable deception for a group of users
Logout Zscaler Client Connector when Zscaler Deception Entitlement is Enabled

prose.text: {{integration}} The per-device Deception Settings password is in [[zcc.passwords-and-otp.otp]]. What the disable password and Sync do is open {{gap:password-and-sync}}.

prose.label: Device groups.
prose.text: {{device-groups}} The groups themselves are defined in [[zcc.entitlements.device-groups]].

prose.label: Logging users out.
prose.text: {{logout-option}} The two Deception pages give the option different scopes {{divergence:logout-scope}} and name different services as missing when it is off {{divergence:logout-off-service}}. The ZDX page has the same option for ZDX: [[zcc.entitlements.zdx:logout-on-enable]].

prose.label: When a change lands.
prose.text: {{update-timing}} The two Deception pages name different places for the reauthentication {{divergence:reauth-place}}.

checks.do: Whether Zscaler Deception Enabled by Default is on; if it is, groups cannot be used, otherwise whether the user's group or device group is selected.
Whether the client is Windows 3.9 or later before expecting group-based Deception.
Before telling an admin whom the logout option applies to, which service runs without it, or where users reauthenticate, the divergences rather than either Deception page alone.

integration.statement: Integrating Client Connector with Zscaler Deception enhances Client Connector's ability to manage the Deception process on endpoints; the Admin Console receives Deception configuration updates automatically, Sync updates them manually, and a password can be required to disable Deception.

quotes: Integrating Zscaler Client Connector with Zscaler Deception enhances the ability of Zscaler Client Connector to manage the Deception process on endpoints.

While the Zscaler Admin Console receives automatic configuration updates from Deception, you can click Sync to manually update Deception configurations. You can also require a password to disable Deception.

windows-3-9.statement: Enabling Deception for a select group of users or for device groups needs Client Connector 3.9 or later for Windows.

quotes: To enable Deception for only a select group of users, you must deploy Zscaler Client Connector for Windows 3.9 or later.
To enable Deception for device groups, you must install Zscaler Client Connector for Windows 3.9 or later.

default-switch.statement: Deception is assigned to a group of users or to device groups only with Zscaler Deception Enabled by Default disabled; if it is enabled, Deception is available for all users and cannot be assigned to a group or a device group.

quotes: To enable Deception for only a group of users, ensure that Zscaler Deception Enabled by Default is disabled. If this setting is enabled, Deception is available for all users and you cannot assign Deception to a group.

To enable Deception for device groups, ensure that Zscaler Deception Enabled by Default is disabled. If this setting is enabled, Deception is available for all users and you cannot assign Deception to a device group.

groups-default.statement: By default no groups are selected, which indicates that no groups have access to Deception and allows users to keep their current settings; if groups do not appear, the page says to ensure they are synced between Internet & SaaS and Client Connector.

quotes: By default, no groups are selected, which indicates that no groups have access to Deception
allows users to keep their current settings.
If you do not see your groups, ensure that groups are synced between Internet & SaaS and Zscaler Client Connector.

configurations.statement: With Zscaler Deception Enabled by Default enabled, Deception is enabled for all users; disabled with no groups specified, it is disabled for users; disabled with groups specified, it is enabled only for the specified groups.

quotes: | Enabled | N/A | Deception service is enabled for all users |
| Disabled | No | Deception service disabled for users |
| Disabled | Yes | Deception service is enabled only for the specified group of users |

device-groups.statement: Configuring Deception for device groups assigns entitlements and policy settings based on ownership through device posture profiles; the vendor's example enrolls a personal device in Deception and an employer-provided device in Deception and Private Access.

quotes: Configuring Deception for device groups allows you to assign entitlements and policy settings based on ownership through device posture profiles.
The personal device can be enrolled in Deception and the employer-provided device can be enrolled in Deception and Private Access.

logout-option.statement: On the Deception for device groups page, Logout Zscaler Client Connector when Zscaler Deception Entitlement is Enabled automatically logs users out of Client Connector when Deception is enabled for a device group, and users can then log in again to enable the Deception service.

quotes: Select Logout Zscaler Client Connector when Zscaler Deception Entitlement is Enabled to automatically log users out of Zscaler Client Connector when Deception is enabled for a device group. Users can then log in again to enable the Deception service.

update-timing.statement: On the Deception for user groups page, users' devices are updated the next time they connect and, if already connected, automatically in 60 minutes; users can instead click Update Policy from the More window, after which they must reauthenticate in the Zscaler Deception Service Status window.

quotes: Your users' devices are updated the next time they connect. If users are already connected, devices automatically update in 60 minutes.
To manually update devices, users can go into Zscaler Client Connector and click Update Policy from the More window.
After manually refreshing, users must reauthenticate in the Zscaler Deception Service Status window.

logout-scope.summary: The two Deception entitlement pages give the logout option different scopes: the device groups page says it applies to customers using Private Access only, the user groups page to customers using Private Access only or Private Access and Deception.

quotes: This applies to customers using Private Access only.

positions.says: Deception for device groups: the option applies to customers using Private Access only.

quotes: This applies to customers using Private Access only or Private Access and Deception.

positions.says: Deception for user groups: the option applies to customers using Private Access only or Private Access and Deception.

logout-scope.impact: Whether a customer using Private Access and Deception is covered by the logout option depends on which page is read.

logout-off-service.summary: With the logout option off, the device groups page says Client Connector runs without the Deception service until the next login, while the user groups page names the Digital Experience service.

quotes: When not enabled, Zscaler Client Connector runs without the Deception service until the next Zscaler Client Connector login.

positions.says: Deception for device groups: without the option, the app runs without the Deception service until the next login.

quotes: When disabled, Zscaler Client Connector runs without the Digital Experience service until the next Zscaler Client Connector login.

positions.says: Deception for user groups: without the option, the app runs without the Digital Experience service until the next login.

logout-off-service.impact: The user groups page names Digital Experience in a Deception article, so the service that stays off until the next login is not settled by the pages; the ZDX page has the same sentence for ZDX.

reauth-place.summary: After Update Policy for a Deception change, the user groups page has users reauthenticate in the Zscaler Deception Service Status window and the device groups page on the Private Access page.

quotes: After manually refreshing, users must reauthenticate in the Zscaler Deception Service Status window.

positions.says: Deception for user groups: users reauthenticate in the Zscaler Deception Service Status window.

quotes: After manually refreshing the device, they must reauthenticate on the Private Access page.

positions.says: Deception for device groups: users reauthenticate on the Private Access page.

reauth-place.impact: Which window a user reauthenticates in after refreshing the policy is not settled by the pages: each names a different place, and neither says the two differ in the product.

password-and-sync.title: Where the Deception disable password is configured and what Sync pulls
password-and-sync.detail: The integration page says a password can be required to disable Deception and that Sync manually updates Deception configurations, without saying where the password is set or which configuration Sync retrieves. The page it refers to, 'Deploying Endpoint Deception with Zscaler Client Connector for Windows', is not in this area.

other-platforms.title: Deception entitlement on platforms other than Windows
other-platforms.detail: Both Deception entitlement pages give a Windows 3.9 floor and say nothing about macOS, Linux or mobile.
